title: LLM-first pipeline — Approach B (placeholder)
description:
Placeholder story for Approach B: an LLM-first pipeline where the LLM derives structure directly from raw source files, rather than enriching a heuristic skeleton.

## What Approach B means

Instead of running a heuristic skeleton first and then having the LLM enrich it, Approach B feeds the raw source files (or batches of them) directly to an LLM and asks it to produce the L1→L4 hierarchy, grouping decisions, semantic names, and descriptions in one or more passes.

```
source files
     ↓
 LLM analyses all files (batched)
     ↓
 LLM proposes L1→L4 hierarchy directly
     ↓
 post-validation pass against structural rules
     ↓
 enriched knowledge  ←→  golden-standard.json (oracle)
```

## Why features are deliberately not written yet

Approach B's features depend heavily on what Approach A reveals:
- Which parts of the hierarchy does the heuristic skeleton get right structurally but wrong semantically? Those are the Approach B opportunities.
- Which LLM prompts and structured output contracts work reliably at scale? Approach A's LlmLogicalPieceExtractor and LlmGroupingPass experiments will answer this before Approach B needs them.
- What are the actual per-run costs, latencies, and failure rates of LLM-based extraction? Only measurable after Approach A has a baseline.
- For projects like small-dirty (13 no-op infrastructure classes), does pre-pass LLM file classification beat post-hoc heuristic noise detection? Only answerable with Approach A metrics in hand.

Features for this story should NOT be written until Approach A (story: LLM-enriched pipeline — Approach A) is complete and its convergence metrics are established. At that point, the remaining gaps in Approach A's output will define exactly what Approach B needs to attempt.

## Potential feature areas (not yet specified)

- LLM-first file classification pass (noise vs real code) as a pre-filter before structural extraction
- LLM-derived grouping from raw file content batches (bypassing heuristic skeleton entirely for L2/L3)
- LLM-proposed hierarchy validation and structural rule enforcement post-pass
- Cost/latency/quality comparison harness between Approach A and Approach B outputs on the same fixtures
- Decision: when to fall back from Approach B to Approach A (reliability threshold, token budget, project size)

## Note to future implementer

Do not begin implementing this story until the Approach A story has delivered at least iterations 2 and 3 (LlmLogicalPieceExtractor wired + LlmGroupingPass at L2) and the convergence score against golden-standard.json is recorded. The Approach A score is the baseline that Approach B must beat to justify the added complexity and cost.
